1.explanation:
1. We import the Tabs components from carbon-components-react@7.23.2 and include the Carbon stylesheet.  
2. We render a Tabs component inside a fixed-width container (400px) so that not all tabs can fit side by side. This triggers the overflow behavior of the Tabs component, which renders left/right navigation buttons.  
3. Inspecting the generated DOM for the overflow buttons (class names like `bx--tabs-nav__btn` or `bx--tab-overflow__btn`) reveals that these `<button>` elements have no `aria-label`, `aria-labelledby`, or visible `<label>`, causing the accessibility violation.  
4. This minimal reproducible example shows exactly how to surface the bug in a local application.
1.bug_scenario: When the Carbon React Tabs component is rendered with more tabs than can fit into a narrow viewport, two arrow navigation buttons appear for scrolling through the overflowed tabs. Those arrow buttons are rendered as plain <button> elements containing only an icon and have no aria-label, aria-labelledby, or title attribute. This causes an accessibility violation “Form control element <button> has no associated label.”
